tagline.text: An open-air shopping and dining street in the heart of BGC, with year-end fireworks

location.label: Location
location.text: 5th and 9th Avenues area, Bonifacio Global City (BGC), Taguig

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (holiday lights in November–December)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000–3,500 (per person, with a meal, a café stop and a little shopping)

children.text: Bonifacio High Street is BGC's signature open-air shopping street, opened by Ayala Land in October 2007. You can shop, eat and stroll on foot, and in November–December there is a tree lighting and Saturday fireworks.

Bonifacio High Street (BHS for short) is a pedestrian, open-air shopping street in the middle of Bonifacio Global City (BGC) in Taguig, Metro Manila. Developed by Ayala Land, it opened in October 2007 and has since grown into a series of connected blocks. According to Wikipedia, the first two blocks are open-air shopping streets, the third is High Street Central (partly indoor, with cinemas), and the fourth is High Street South, which mixes retail with residences. High Street Central followed in May 2012, Central Square in June 2014 and One Bonifacio High Street in August 2018.

The appeal here is simply walking. Wide car-free promenades are lined with fashion stores, bookshops, cafés and restaurants, and trees, small parks, benches and outdoor seating make it easy to rest even on a hot day. There is public art too, such as murals and sculptures, and the art program is described as run by the Bonifacio Art Foundation (BAFI). After dark the lights come on and the mood changes, so many visitors split the visit into shopping and cafés by day and dinner and a stroll in the evening.

For travelers, it is a different kind of choice from Ayala Center or Greenbelt in Makati. Instead of a big mall you walk into, the whole street is the mall, so in good weather you can walk for hours without air conditioning. Many locals bring their dogs, which is part of the charm. Just know that while walking the street is free, meals, coffee and shopping cost more than the Manila average. Wikipedia and Cushman & Wakefield's 2024 survey (covering BGC as a whole) list it as the 43rd most expensive retail street in the world.

In November–December the holiday program "HighStreet Holiday" makes the area especially busy. In 2026 the tree lighting took place on November 4 at Bonifacio High Street Park, and Saturday fireworks were announced for 5th Avenue. It is great for photos and atmosphere, but crowds grow, so allow extra travel time. Other events continue beyond the holidays. Run BGC, a running event with 5K, 10K and 16K distances plus a 1K dog run, is scheduled on Bonifacio High Street for Sunday, November 29, 2026, and pop-up markets selling crafts, fashion and small goods are said to appear often on weekends. Dates and venues can change with organizer announcements, so check before you go.

International brands, local boutiques and bookshops line the wide promenade. Large flagship stores such as Nike, Adidas and LEGO are fun just to look at, and there is no admission fee for walking the street. On a map the street runs as four connected blocks, and High Street South at the far end has landscaped parks and a corporate plaza that make quiet corners for photos.

Central Square has MUJI, Shake Shack and The Marketplace supermarket, plus cinemas. It is a good place to step indoors and cool off at midday. Booking movie tickets online is recommended. The nearby Landmark combines a supermarket and a department store, handy for everyday supplies.

blocks.title: The Food District at One Bonifacio High Street

children.text: The lower level of One Bonifacio High Street has a food hall called the Food District, where many restaurants share one space. It is convenient when you travel alone or cannot decide on a menu, and the upper floors include a Spanish restaurant and others.

Well-known names such as Din Tai Fung, Shake Shack, Marugame Udon and Wildflour Cafe + Bakery cluster here. With Japanese, Spanish, Korean and Filipino options, it is easy to find something when your group has different tastes.

This large bookstore, a BGC landmark, sits in the B6 area of High Street and spans four floors. The top floor has a big comics and graphic novel section, and Filipino authors' books and stationery make good souvenirs.
Murals, sculptures and seasonal light installations appear on building walls and in side lanes. Search the #BGCArt hashtag on Instagram to see what is on now, as installations change often.

In November–December the program includes a tree lighting, Saturday fireworks, Simbang Gabi (the nine pre-Christmas masses) at the amphitheater on December 15–23, and Christmas fireworks. The schedule changes every year, so check BGC's official channels. Santa meet-and-greets were also announced for December 6, 13, 20 and 24 at Park Triangle Mall. Saturday fireworks start at 7:30 PM on 5th Avenue.
With lawns and benches, locals bring their dogs for evening walks. Bring a mat if you want to sit on the grass, and ask the owner first if you would like to pet a dog.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: Start in the afternoon and finish in the evening

children.text: Start at the front of High Street and walk along 5th Avenue, looking at the stores and murals. The sun is strong at this hour, so duck into building shade or a café now and then.
Shop and rest at Fully Booked or inside Central Square. If you plan to see a movie, book your seat at this time.
Have an early dinner at the Food District in One Bonifacio High Street or along the 9th Avenue restaurant row. Many places have a wait in the evening.
Stroll slowly down the lit-up street. If it is a Saturday during the holidays, wait on 5th Avenue for the fireworks.

The promenade is long but flat, so it is easy to walk. Just wear comfortable shoes. Market! Market! is generally known to open around 10–11 AM and close around 10 PM (during the 2024 year-end period: 11 AM–10 PM on weekdays, 10 AM–10 PM on weekends). Hours change on holidays and at year-end, so check before you go.

items.title: Full-day route
items.subtitle: Combine it with the rest of BGC

children.text: In the cool morning, visit other BGC sights or a park first. If you want to see The Mind Museum, reserve a time slot (9:00, 12:00 or 3:00).
Have lunch and shop on High Street.
Rest at a nearby café, then finish with dinner and a stroll.
From central Manila (Malate, Ermita) and NAIA Airport, a taxi or Grab is the simplest option. Travel time varies greatly with Manila traffic, so leave plenty of buffer.
From Makati you can reach it quickly by BGC Bus or taxi. It gets congested at rush hour (5–8 PM).
Exact travel times and fares depend on traffic at the time of departure, so confirm locally.
BGC Bus is an inexpensive scheduled bus that runs within BGC and to and from Makati. Guides from 2025–2026 list the regular route fare as about
According to Wikipedia, stops near High Street include One Parkade (routes AS09, C08 and WR10) and Nutriasia (routes AS03 and C02).
Pay with a Beep card or GCash. Routes are revised often, so check the latest announcements.
From the Makati side you can board a BGC Bus at the EDSA Ayala terminal (McKinley Exchange Corporate Center). It is crowded at commuting hours, so allow extra time.
Inside High Street you get around entirely on foot. The blocks connect along 5th and 9th Avenues, so it is hard to get lost.
The dry season from November to May is best for walking. December–February in particular has cool mornings and evenings that make outdoor strolls pleasant.
Holiday events cluster in November–December, so crowds are larger but there is also the most to see. For a quieter walk, choose a weekday morning or afternoon.
As for timing, either start walking in the late morning, or spend the midday indoors and come back out toward sunset. Shade is limited in places, so you take the sun fully at midday.

BGC has many hotels, and staying within walking distance of High Street makes evening strolls easy. Rates run higher than the Manila average, so compare by date.

Many well-known places are here, such as Din Tai Fung, Shake Shack, Marugame Udon and Wildflour. Evenings bring waits, so go early or book ahead. Hours vary by venue and are generally described as about 10 AM to 10 PM.

If you want a quieter stop, Burgos Circle and Forbestown behind High Street are calmer dining and residential areas. In good weather you can walk there, and it suits dinner. If you need a late snack or coffee, some cafés stay open late, so check hours locally.
The sun is strong in the daytime, so bring a hat, sunscreen and water.
For restaurants that fill up in the evening, going right at opening or early keeps the wait short.
Pair it with other BGC sights such as The Mind Museum to build a full day. The museum is closed on Mondays, so check ahead.
Holiday and weekend fireworks and events cause traffic jams, so prefer public transport and walking.
Taxi and Grab fares can change by time of day, so check the fare in the app beforehand.
Murals and light installations change, so look up the #BGCArt hashtag on Instagram for the latest displays before you go.
Many dogs are out here, so get the owner's permission before petting one.
On holiday event days and weekend evenings it gets very crowded, so keep your belongings secure and allow extra travel time.
Event schedules, fireworks dates and opening hours change every year, so check BGC's official channels.
In the rainy season, showers and typhoons may cancel outdoor events.
BGC Bus routes are revised often, and some routes were reported to be under adjustment in 2026. Check the latest route map.
Keep your phone and wallet in a front pocket or the inside of your bag, as petty theft can occur in busy areas.
Parking rates and availability differ by building, so check before you arrive, and avoid driving if you can.
Pop-up markets or events may close part of the walkway, so follow on-site signs and detour around them.
This is the urban district that contains High Street, with parks, art and restaurants. Within the district you get around on foot or by BGC Bus.
A mall in nearby McKinley Hill with canals modeled on Venice. You can combine gondola rides and shopping.
An open-air shopping complex in Makati that offers a different version of the same open-street atmosphere. Travel time varies greatly with traffic, so check in an app.
A World War II memorial cemetery near BGC, where you can reflect on history in a quiet atmosphere.
A science museum in BGC with more than 250 interactive exhibits. It is open Tuesday–Sunday, 9 AM–6 PM, and closed Mondays. Check the latest announcements for admission and promotions.
